1.support: Objective: To investigate the effects of three titration methods on right heart function and prognosis in patients with ARDS.

2.support: A total of 62 ARDS patients hospitalized between April 2020 and December 2021 in the Department of Intensive Care Medicine, Shaanxi Provincial People's Hospital, China were enrolled into an observational prospective study.

3.support: Fig 2 flow chart: 101 screened, 70 met inclusion criteria, 8 excluded for incomplete data, 62 included; participation among those meeting inclusion was 62/70 (89%).

4.support: Inclusion criteria were as follows: 1) patients aged 18-75 years; 2) requirement for mechanical ventilation for a duration greater than 3 days; 3) met the diagnostic criteria of the 2012 Berlin definition of ARDS.

5.support: The report contains no sample size calculation, power description, or variance/effect estimate justification for the 62 enrolled patients; the discussion attributes null findings to 'the small study sample' but no a priori sizing.

6.support: Patients were divided into the guide (G) group, the transpulmonary pressure-oriented (TPO) group and the driving pressure-oriented (DPO) group at enrollment, with echocardiography and outcomes assessed at 24, 48 and 72 hours and 28-day mortality thereafter.

7.support: TTE was repeated within 24, 48, and 72 hours after initiating mechanical ventilation, respectively, and 28-day mortality was recorded, a timeframe in which PEEP effects on right heart function can plausibly appear.
7.location: Page 3, Echocardiographic assessment; Page 3, Blood gas analysis

8.support: ARDS patients were enrolled into three distinct PEEP-Driving pressure titration strategies groups: guide, transpulmonary pressure-oriented and driving pressure-oriented.

9.support: An esophageal balloon catheter was inserted... Esophageal pressure (Pes) was monitored to indirectly reflect intrathoracic pressure... PEEP was reduced from 20 cm H2O by 2 cm H2O increments until a value of 6 cm H2O.

10.support: The exposure is the fixed assignment to one of three PEEP titration strategies ('There was no crossover between the three strategies'), applied once at enrollment; repeated measurement of the exposure itself is not applicable, though ventilatory parameters were remeasured at 24, 48 and 72 h.

11.support: Right ventricular systolic dysfunction was defined as TAPSE < 16 mm... In addition, tricuspid E/A < 0.8 indicates impaired diastole. RV dilatation was defined by a RVEDA/LVEDA ratio >0.6.
11.location: Page 3, Blood gas analysis / endpoint definitions

12.support: Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) was performed on admission by specialists (DDR WY and RJW)... The report does not state whether these outcome assessors were blinded to the PEEP titration group.

13.support: All 62 patients had an initial PEEP value of 5 cm H2O... The current cohort experienced 31 patient deaths, giving a mortality rate of 50% with no significant difference among groups (p=0.368); no losses to follow-up after enrollment are reported.

14.support: Multivariate logistic regression analysis with right heart dysfunction was analyzed by logistic regression analysis (backward stepwise selection algorithm)... such as PEEP titration methods, Vt, Pmean, compliance, PEEP, respiratory rate, PaCO2, pH, driving pressure and transpulmonary pressure end-inspiratory.

nih.rationale: Driven by item 5 (no sample size or power justification), item 12 (no blinding of the echocardiographic outcome assessors to titration group), and the non-randomized, physician-discretion allocation to the three exposure groups (item 4 is met for criteria but allocation itself may introduce selection bias, reflected in baseline differences such as age and compliance). Strengths include a clear objective, prespecified eligibility criteria, prospective exposure measurement with a validated esophageal pressure protocol, objectively defined outcomes, complete 28-day follow-up, and multivariate adjustment for key confounders, which prevent a Poor rating but fall short of Good.
